Basically, anything not related to the actual technical process of making fakes (although certain technical aspects could be mentioned).

To start the discussion, from what I've seen is that model likeness to celeb is super important. However, the caveat to this would be if the models head shape matches up as well. I'm curious to find what tips others would give to aspiring deepfakers...

I think the three most important things are:

1) quality of training data: Blurred or obstructed faces should be tossed from your training set. A few hundred quality images will get you better results than 5,000 crappy images.

2) model selection: You touched on this one and it's important. Your models should be as similar as possible if you are aiming for realism. Head shape is probs the most important aspect of this. Trying to swap a face from a round faced person to someone with a long narrow face is not ever going to look good. Skin tone can be a factor too.

3) Realistic expectations: Thinking that this software is perfect and ready to go out of the box is a total fantasy. We're a long way off. Thinking that you can dive into this without some intermediate knowledge and computer troubleshooting skills probably will be a very frustrating journey for you. Also, thinking that you can crank out a perfect video in a day using a graphics card from 2014 is a mistake. This stuff takes a lot of time and trial and error.

Good points all around! I also think people don't try to vary the celeb facial expressions enough. The worst is when you got a good deepfake going and she leaned back and the effect is totally lost. I suppose if the pornstar looks similar already, it may mask this but when it's bad... ITS BAD.

Anyway, rdcy fakes on Tumblr found a scene where Gal Gadot tilts her head back and closes her eyes. He used it for a headswap but it's exactly the kind of thing more deepfakers need to have in their arsenal if they are ever going to take it to the next level

In general for newbies though, the big thing is that they look as close as possible in the scene being used. In terms of hair and (mainly) head shape but if you're not as skilled at training; the face shape needs to be a doppelganger as well. That's just what I've noticed from observation.

Also: training too long can result in overtraining, causing a reversal back to the original model. Training way longer does not mean it will be better.

Gather multiple videos, slow down the frame rate by a lot and try to gather frames (I try to get 3-7k frames but that's because I have a powerful machine) I know from personal experience that you cannot get away with having 1 long ass video even if you have sliced the fps by a lot. the problem with having too little videos is that you will not diversify the lighting and emotions (unless its a vlog were the person is moving and changing)

2. Makeup can be a pain in the ass, if its a celebrity, try to get pictures that match makeup (this goes for the porn actress too)

3. have a good quality in the faces you've gatterd for extra details the bot can pick up on.

4. Recycle your model, what I mean by this is that when you start a new project, do not delete the old model. use the same one (The bot already knows angles of faces, lighting and face structures so even if you put a whole other face the bot will adapt.

5. Lighting and emotions, like I've mention before, it is very important. try to get shots with different lighting, angles and emotions so the bot can have a feel of the face and model it more accurately.

Common mistakes

  1. You know in some videos the skin of the face does not match the body? that's due to the faces the bot trained with did not contain diverse lighting and or not extreme lighting like that video

  2. You start up the PC after days and days of training and you see that the bot has reached 0.001 loss value. Great! In reality this is what you call overfitting and its basically the bot did not actually lean to model the face, rather it learned to copy and paste the faces that you presented. to solve this, or to see if you've overfitted, is adding more faces the bot can train with. this is why you want 1-3k AT LEAST of faces in your aligned folder.

  3. Unmatching faces. Understanding what the program is doing. a common misconception is that you're copy and pasting a face into a body. the program is not doing that, rather it is merging both faces into a single one and creating a hybrid face, that's why you may see fakes that do not look like the celebrity. you want to combat this by getting a pornstar that looks like your celebrity aswell as having a very similar bone structure. (Trust me, it's a pain in the ass to revert all your progress because a shitty match.) Find porn stars with pornstarbyface.com and other dooplebahger platforms.

  4. Do not feature a blowjob scene. putting a dick in the mouth of your model is not a good idea because the bot will not know what the fuck is happening and it will just flip out and not do its job. do not try get it to work because it will not.

  5. Do not use pictures. there are programs out there that will rip out a bunch of photos of a keyword. say you type Emma Stone and the it will gather 3000+ pictures from that keyword. this is a terrible idea because it might pick up on photos that are unrelated, have other people on it, feature underage pictures of model, and probably will have a shit load of makeup on them.

  6. DO NOT gather poor pictures. it's better to have 1000 good faces than 3000 faces that are bad. Don't be lazy and actually put in some work if you want great results
